ai.title: Fix Windows line endings in main-prompt
ai.summary: Normalize line endings for new file content before diff generation in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`. Export `processFileBlock` to enable unit testing. Add `backend/src/__tests__/main-prompt.test.ts` to verify normalization logic. Internal refactor affecting backend prompt processing.

eli5.text: When the system compares your old and new file content to show you what changed, it now converts Windows-style line breaks to the standard format before doing the comparison, so diffs come out consistent regardless of which operating system created the file. This keeps the displayed changes from showing spurious differences caused only by line-ending style. You'd notice cleaner, more accurate change listings when working with files that originated on Windows. The fix is live as of today in the backend prompt processing.

ai.title: Add root start script
ai.summary: Added `start` script to root `package.json`. Delegates to `npm-app` workspace. Internal tooling only.

eli5.text: Running the project is now one command instead of opening a subfolder first. You type "start" at the top level, and it automatically launches the assistant interface without needing to navigate into its folder. This only affects developers building the software, not anyone using the finished tool.

ai.title: Print generating files message earlier in CLI
ai.summary: Moved the 'Generating file changes' console log from `npm-app/src/cli.ts` to `npm-app/src/client.ts`. The message now prints immediately when the response stream ends and contains the `STOP_MARKER` plus `</file>`, rather than waiting for the full response to be awaited. This provides faster feedback to the user during file generation.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to create or modify files, you'll now see the "Generating file changes. Please wait..." message appear sooner instead of waiting until everything is fully done. This gives you faster feedback that your request is being processed.

ai.title: CLI uses readline module
ai.summary: The CLI now utilizes the Node.js `readline` module for input handling, replacing custom raw-mode key processing. This update enables standard terminal features such as command history navigation via Up/Down arrows and cursor movement via Left/Right arrows. The `ChatStorage.navigateVersion` method signature changed from accepting 'left'/'right' to 'undo'/'redo', aligning with new `Ctrl+Z`/`Ctrl+Y` bindings for file version control. Changes affect `npm-app/src/cli.ts` and `npm-app/src/chat-storage.ts`.

eli5.text: When you type commands in the assistant, the up and down arrow keys now let you scroll back through things you've already typed, and the left and right arrows move your cursor within the current line so you can edit what you're typing. Pressing Ctrl+Z takes you back to an earlier version of your work file, and Ctrl+Y moves you forward again. These changes affect anyone using the command-line version of the assistant, and you'd notice the typing feels smoother and more like a standard terminal when you use it.

ai.title: Bump version to 1.0.15
ai.summary: Incremented `manicode` package version from 1.0.14 to 1.0.15 in `npm-app/package.json`. This change updates the internal version identifier for the CLI application. No functional code or dependencies were modified.

eli5.text: The internal version label for the assistant's command-line tool quietly moved up one tiny notch, like a car's odometer rolling from mile 14 to mile 15. Only the people who build and ship the tool will notice the difference because it doesn't change how the tool works today. It's the software equivalent of updating a library's catalog card number before reshelving the book.

ai.title: CLI undo redo commands
ai.summary: CLI keybindings for file version control switched from Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y to Ctrl+U/Ctrl+R. Internal handler methods renamed to handleUndo/handleRedo to match new semantics. Text commands `undo`, `redo`, `quit`, `exit`, and `q` added to input parser. Covers npm-app/src/cli.ts and npm-app/knowledge.md.

eli5.text: If you use the command-line version of the tool, the keyboard shortcuts for stepping backward and forward through your file's saved versions have changed: undo is now Ctrl+U and redo is now Ctrl+R (previously Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y). The same undo and redo actions can now also be typed as text commands, just like you already could type quit or exit to leave the program. These changes apply to the internal command-line interface used by the team and are live today in the current build.

ai.title: Update menu instructions
ai.summary: Updated `npm-app/src/menu.ts` to clarify keyboard shortcuts and tip formatting. Changed exit instructions to specify ESC for closing and CTRL-C for exiting. Updated undo/redo tips to reference CTRL-U and CTRL-R instead of arrow keys.

eli5.text: When you open the assistant's on-screen menu, the wording for buttons and shortcuts is clearer: it now tells you to press ESC to close the menu and CTRL-C to exit, and the tips about undoing or redoing changes say to use CTRL-U and CTRL-R instead of the old arrow-key instructions. You'd notice friendlier, more accurate labels the next time you bring up the menu while the program is running.

ai.title: System prompt: planning block becomes brainstorm block
ai.summary: Renamed the <planning> block to <brainstorm> in backend/src/system-prompt.ts. The instruction now asks the agent to consider possible plans, check for a better alternative to the first idea, and choose the best one before proceeding. Internal prompt-only change; no user-facing commands or model behavior contracts altered.

eli5.text: The assistant's internal instruction manual, which guides how it thinks through solving your problem, now explicitly tells it to consider multiple possible approaches rather than just jumping to the first plan that comes to mind. This is a behind-the-scenes change that only affects how the assistant is prompted; you as the user won't notice any different behavior today, but the assistant is internally guided to think more flexibly before acting.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.16
ai.summary: Incremented `manicode` package version from 1.0.15 to 1.0.16 in `npm-app/package.json`. Marked Windows-specific input and edit failures as resolved in `musings.knowledge.md`.

eli5.text: Internal documentation was updated to mark four Windows-specific problems as resolved: backspace not clearing characters, left arrow keys not working, edits failing to apply, and Ctrl-C not functioning. These issues had been recorded earlier but now show as checked off, indicating the team considers them addressed in the current version of the software. If you looked at the project, you wouldn't see any visible changes, just a note that these Windows quirks are no longer open items.

ai.title: Disable chat persistence to filesystem
ai.summary: Chat persistence to the local filesystem is disabled in `npm-app/src/chat-storage.ts`. The `fs.writeFileSync` call within `saveChat` is commented out, preventing chat data from being serialized to disk. This change affects the internal storage mechanism for the npm-app package.

eli5.text: The assistant no longer saves copies of your conversations to a local file on the computer it runs on. If you were looking for a record of a past chat stored on disk, you won't find one, because the program now skips writing that file entirely.
